title: Hallo! Hoe gaat het?
goal: Greet people and say goodbye, informally and formally; ask how someone is and answer; say who you are with ik ben and ik heet.

content.text: Sofia is from Spain and has a new job in Utrecht. Today she arrives in the Netherlands, and she will live in her friend Noor's flat for now. In this lesson you will learn to say hello and goodbye, ask how someone is, and say who you are.
In this lesson, the subject of a sentence is
Sofia lands at Schiphol and takes the train to Utrecht Centraal. Noor is waiting for her at the station.

turns.speaker: Sofia
turns.text: Goed, dank je. Ik ben een beetje moe. En met jou?

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Met mij gaat het heel goed!

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Ja, Utrecht Centraal is heel groot.

words.note: The formal pair of dank je (wel).

words.meaning: How are you? How's it going? (to anyone)

words.note: Joins a question or sentence to what came before.

words.meaning: And you? (asking the same question back, informal)

words.example: Met mij gaat het heel goed!
words.note: Fixed word order; do not take it apart yet.

words.example: Met mij gaat het heel goed!
Ja, Utrecht Centraal is heel groot.

content.text: Dutch has a different greeting for each part of the day.
is both hello and goodbye — neutral, and fine with everyone.
It never means "good night" — for that, use welterusten.
are the same rough sound at the back of the throat:

words.note: Works both ways — neutral, fine with everyone.
One word. Never used at bedtime.

words.note: Same moment as welterusten; both are fine.

props.translation: Is it going well? No, not so good.

blocks.content: zijn: ik ben, jij bent, u bent, hij/zij is

content.text: means "to be". These are its singular forms — the forms for wij, jullie and zij (plural) come in the next lesson.

props.note: A name behaves like hij/zij, so is.

content.text: is formal: strangers, older people, a counter or reception.
Dutch people use jij a lot — friends, family, children, colleagues, often even the boss.
is a bit more formal. To ask:

props.translation: My name is Sofia. / I'm called Sofia.
props.note: heten is explained in a later lesson; for now, learn it as a chunk.
A fixed chunk; asked at the door in the next story scene.
More formal than Ik heet …; mijn is a fixed chunk here.

content.text: When you meet someone new in the Netherlands, shake hands and say your first name. Friends and family often give three kisses on the cheek (right–left–right) or a hug. "Hoe gaat het?" usually gets a short answer.
In the afternoon, at the front door of Noor's flat, Sofia and Noor meet Noor's elderly neighbour, Els.

turns.speaker: Noor
turns.text: Hallo Els! Hoe gaat het met u?

turns.speaker: Els
turns.text: Prima, dank je. En wie ben jij?

turns.speaker: Els
turns.text: Dag Sofia. Ik ben Els, de buurvrouw.

content.text: to them. Older people often say je to younger people, but you keep saying u until they offer jij
(the next lesson has Zeg maar jij.)
. Notice Noor even uses Els's first name together with u — that is normal in Dutch.

content.text: That evening, before bed, Noor and Sofia say good night.

props.note: Said at bedtime, recycled from the Goodbyes section.
Also fine instead of Slaap lekker!.
Sofia's first full day at work is tomorrow.

blocks.content: Fill in ben, bent or is

data.instruction: Fill in ben, bent or is. Example: Ik (zijn) Sofia → ben.

items.note: ik → ben.
jij/je → bent.
u → bent, the same as jij.
A name works like hij/zij, so is.
hij/zij or a name → is.
ik → ben (Ik heet Sofia also works, but this drills zijn).
Ze (= Els) is hij/zij, so is.

data.instruction: Complete the short exchanges. Fill in one word per blank. Example: Hoe … het? → gaat.

items.prompt: Noor: Hoi Sofia! Hoe … het? / Sofia: Goed, … je. En met …?
items.note: Fixed chunks: Hoe gaat het?, dank je, En met jou?

items.prompt: Receptioniste: Goedemorgen! Hoe gaat het met …? / Sofia: Goed, … u wel.
items.note: Formal exchange: met u, dank u.

items.prompt: Els: Goedemiddag! / Noor: Hallo Els! Hoe gaat het met …? / Els: Prima, … je.
items.note: Noor says u to Els; Els answers with dank je (she says je to younger people).

items.prompt: Sofia: Ik … moe. / Noor: Welterusten! Slaap …!
items.note: Ik ben; Slaap lekker! is a fixed goodnight chunk.

items.prompt: Noor: Tot ziens, Sofia! / Sofia: Doei! Tot …!
items.note: tot morgen = see you tomorrow.

data.instruction: Put the words in order. Write the full sentence. Example: Sofia / is / moe → Sofia is moe.

items.prompt: Put in order: ben / ik / Sofia
items.note: Subject + verb + rest: Ik ben Sofia.

items.prompt: Put in order: moe / ben / een beetje / ik
items.note: ik always comes first in a statement.

items.prompt: Put in order: gaat / hoe / het
items.note: Question word first, then the verb.

items.prompt: Put in order: heet / ik / Noor
items.note: Subject + verb + rest.

items.prompt: Put in order: is / Els / de buurvrouw
items.note: Subject (Els) + verb (is) + rest.

data.instruction: Rewrite each informal sentence in the formal form. Example: Hoi! → Goedemorgen! / Goedemiddag! / Goedenavond!

items.note: hoi works any time; goedemorgen is time-specific and formal-friendly.
Also fine: Dag! works for both registers.
Also fine: Ik heet Sofia. / Ik ben Sofia.

items.prompt: Welke twee manieren om afscheid te nemen staan in de berichtjes?
items.note: afscheid nemen = to say goodbye; answer: the two goodbyes used.

passage.title: Op Schiphol
passage.content:
Sofia: Hoi Noor! Ik ben op Schiphol.
Noor: Hoi Sofia! Welkom in Nederland! Hoe gaat het?
Sofia: Goed! Ik ben een beetje moe.
Noor: Ik ben straks op Utrecht Centraal.
Sofia: Super! Tot straks!
Noor: Tot straks! Doei!

data.instruction: You meet a new neighbour in the afternoon. Write 4–6 short lines: greet, say your name, ask how they are, say goodbye. Use u.

items.prompt: You meet a new neighbour in the afternoon. Write 4–6 short lines: greet, say your name, ask how they are, say goodbye. Use u.
authorsVersion: Goedemiddag! / Buurman: Goedemiddag! Wie bent u? / Ik ben Sofia. / Buurman: Aangenaam. Ik heet Peter. / Aangenaam. Hoe gaat het met u? / Buurman: Goed, dank u. Tot ziens! / Tot ziens!
items.note: Model answer. de buurman = the (male) neighbour, the pair of de buurvrouw.

content.text: Greetings by time of day: goedemorgen, goedemiddag, goedenavond; dag = hello and goodbye.
zijn: ik ben, jij/u bent, hij/zij is.
jij/je with friends and family, u for formal situations.
